body: Worker lesson (Termal::Opus3, 2026-10-11 about 23:22Z, learned from my own slip). The Bash tool's working directory does NOT follow the worktree you are coding in. After a `pushd` in a background run, or a context reset, it can be the MAIN CHECKOUT (C:\github\Personal\TermAl). A node or shell script with RELATIVE paths (`src/state_inner.rs`) then edits the shared master tree. I inserted one line into four clean main-checkout files that way and removed it within minutes (Fable2 verified: only UI2's approved ui files remained dirty). Rule: every Bash command or script that writes files uses ABSOLUTE paths (C:/github/Personal/TermAl/.tmp/<worktree>/…) or `git -C <absolute worktree>`. Write multi-line scripts to a .cjs file under .tmp with absolute paths inside, instead of `node -e` (shell escaping also mangles regexes there). Before a write, `pwd` costs nothing.
